correctness.rationale: The Celani–Nagy–Zuluaga Botero dual-frame and congruence theorems were inspected at the level of their hypotheses and conclusions. On a chain, both relation conditions give exactly nondecreasing suffix thresholds. Direct upset calculations yield the stated two connective reconstructions and \(\Diamond\dashv\Box\). The undirected relation has one hub-connected component and precisely \(\max(0,t_0-a)\) isolates when nonempty. Summation over active rows yields each rank multiplicity and the explicit \(n=1\) exception. The standalone verifier independently checks all ten algebraic axioms to dual size seven, direct convex congruences to dual size four, and the exhaustive three-element algebra-table case. Limits: finite tests are not the proof, and the published duality is an input.

The older finite weak-Heyting enumeration source addresses a single binary connective; only its abstract could be inspected, so it remains a risk. The central-binomial total count is known and not separately claimed original; the exact WHB congruence-rank distribution plus unary reconstruction is the candidate novelty. Searches in mathematical literature, analogous formulations, a published-result database and the current/prior local claim corpus found no dominating statement. value.rationale: The outcome is a complete classification of the full two-connective semantics on an essential finite Gödel-chain test family. It determines exactly when modal unary data recovers both connectives, every congruence-lattice rank and asymptotic generic simplicity. The Boolean-rank distribution is a natural invariant necessary to classify quotient behavior, not an arbitrary finite slice; the central binomial enumeration alone would be insufficient value.
